historical_record.description: California School of Fine Arts, designed by Bakewell & Brown.
The California School of Fine Arts extended to designs by John Bakewell Jr.
Émigré artist Victor Arnautoff painted three lunettes in the library reading room of what was then the California School of Fine Arts, later the San Francisco Art Institute.

The city's survey names the San Francisco School of Fine Arts, now the San Francisco Art Institute (San Francisco Landmark No. 85) at this address among the bars, cafes, bookshops and clubs of the North Beach Beat scene, whose period of significance it sets at about 1950 to 1965.
The Office of the Assessor-Recorder photographed the property for tax assessment.
Photographed, showing the San Francisco Art Institute.
The San Francisco Art Institute addition, designed 1968-69 by Paffard Keatinge-Clay.

historic_survey.survey: Modern & Postmodern Architectural Styles Historic Context Statement (2024)
historic_survey.note: The San Francisco Art Institute addition by Paffard Keatinge-Clay, one of the best local examples of Brutalism. The building's local landmark designation does not explicitly recognise the addition, though the National Register nomination does. David Ireland's Smithsonian Falls, Descending a Staircase for P.K. was installed in its stairwell in 1987, and the founding members of the Organization of Women Architects were photographed on its roof in 1973.

unknowns: The Modern design context statement dates the Art Institute addition to 1968-69 in one appendix and 1970 in another.
